newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SEEN RECOVERING ON U.S. UNIT.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SEEN RECOVERING ON U.S. UNIT.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted easier on the U.S. dollar on Monday morning but dealers expected it start recovering after a free-fall stretching over a week on the back of import pressure.

"According to the (central) Reserve Bank there's Z$224 million in the market so we should see rates starting to come down slightly," one dealer said, adding that most players were gravitating back towards the normal one-point bid/offer spread after widening as far as 20 points at one stage under pressure.
At around 0810 GMT the local dollar was trading at 11.6000/6500 against the U.S. dollar compared to 11.5700/6700 on Friday but was firmer on sterling at 18.8850/19.0110 from 19.0170/0230.
It was at 6.2215/2625 from 6.3130/3175 versus the mark and at 2.4895/5055 from 2.5290/5325 against South Africa's rand.
